subject: Performance qualification: SLO targets, prompt handoff, and reproducibility plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Diaz <alice.diaz@fastretail.com>; Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 17:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: perf qualification kickoff — SLOs, prompt handoff, reproducibility

Thanks for the call earlier today — quick recap and clear next steps so we can move to a hands-on benchmark smoothly. I summarized the acceptance criteria and what we need from FastRetail to reproduce your peak/steady workloads in our harness.

Top-level acceptance targets (as discussed):
- Latency: p95 <= 60ms, p99 <= 150ms for single-request (non-streaming) flows at profile QPS.
- Throughput: steady-state 180–220 qps sustained for 10m windows; burst to 400 qps for 30s.
- Concurrency: support for 100 concurrent sessions with KV-cache warmup behavior documented.
- Streaming: first-byte <= 300ms, token-lag tail p95 <= 200ms for 1–3 token increments; uninterrupted stream for 60s sessions.

What Redwood will provide this week:
1) benchmark-harness-template.yaml (attached) — how we configure workloads, sampling, and measurement windows.
2) FR_prompt_seed_v1.jsonl (attached) — canonical prompt seeds we used in initial sims. These are a starting point; we’ll accept sanitized variants from you.
3) measurement definitions doc (linked) — exact metric names we’ll capture (server-side and client-side).

What we need from FastRetail (action items):
- Deliver a sanitized sample of production traffic (anonymized request/response pairs) — Tom, you mentioned a 5k-sample export; please drop a zipped copy to the Drive link.
- Confirm any hard SLO blockers (e.g., strict p95 <= 40ms for checkout flows) so we can scope testing.
- Flag which model variants are allowed (open to Redwood recommendations: quantized 8-bit vs fp16) and whether semantic fidelity guardrails are required.

Proposed timeline:
- By Tue 03/07: FR supplies sanitized sample + note of absolute SLO constraints.
- Wed 03/08: Redwood ingests sample, runs initial replay (smoke) against dev harness, shares a short readout.
- Week of 03/13: full benchmark runs and readout; runbook + reproducibility package handed over.

Next step: please upload the sample to the Drive folder (link below) and we’ll sync on Tue if anything blocks ingestion.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cFR-benchmark-artifacts
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/FR-2028-014

Attachments: benchmark-harness-template.yaml (config stub), FR_prompt_seed_v1.jsonl (prompt seeds)

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0124
From: Alice Diaz <alice.diaz@fastretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@fastretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Mar 2028 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: perf qualification kickoff — SLOs, prompt handoff, reproducibility

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. Quick clarifications from our side:
1) The checkout-critical flow is the one we’re most sensitive about. Our product team wants p95 <= 50ms; p99 we can accept up to 200ms but prefer lower. If you can show p95 <= 50ms we’re in a good place.
2) We will provide a 5k-sample sanitized export (headers removed, PII redacted). Tom will upload to the Drive by EOD Tue.
3) Model variants: we are open to Redwood’s recommendation but need fidelity checks against our golden prompt set — if quantization degrades key outputs for intents A/B/C, we’ll need to record a fidelity delta.

One ask: can you include a short repro checklist that someone on our infra team can run locally (container + script) so we can reproduce runs inside our VPC if we need to? That will help procurement and security to confirm the results independently.

We’re also OK with the proposed timeline; let’s aim for the smoke run Wed and the full window the following week.

Thanks — Alice
Alice Diaz
Head of AI Platform, FastRetail
alice.diaz@fastretail.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Diaz <alice.diaz@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 07 Mar 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: perf qualification kickoff — SLOs, prompt handoff, reproducibility

Appreciate the clarity, Alice — and great to hear Tom will upload the sample. A few clarifications and commitments from Redwood:

1) Repro checklist: yes — attached to the Drive folder is a small reproducibility script (run_repro.sh) in the harness template. We’ll also export a Dockerfile and instructions so your infra team can run the same harness inside a VPC. If you want, Marissa will schedule a short handoff session with your infra engineer to walk through permissions and the container image.

2) Fidelity checks: our evaluation harness calculates a pairwise fidelity delta against your golden prompt set (BLEU / ROUGE / semantic-similarity score and an intent-match accuracy). We will include the scoring thresholds we used and the exact prompt inputs in the reproducibility package. If quantization moves you beyond your accepted delta we’ll flag it and propose mitigation (larger model, higher precision quant, or prompt reformulation).

3) Measurement points we will deliver in the readout:
- Server-side: queue depth, token generation time, kernel fallback events, GPU utilization, batch size distribution.
- Client-side: TTFB, per-token latency, stream continuity events, end-to-end action latency (checkout completion).

Operational assignments:
- Marissa Cole: benchmark run coordinator — responsible for running the harness, generating artifact bundle, and scheduling the readout.
- Ben Carter: measurement definitions and SLA verification — will draft the acceptance matrix we use in the readout.
- Karthik: solutions owner — will run the smoke replay and lead the readout.

I’ll mark Marissa and Ben on the HubSpot task. If Tom’s upload completes today we’ll ingest overnight and run a smoke replay Wed morning PST.

Links: HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deal/FR-2028-014
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cFR-benchmark-artifacts
Jira: SUP-3421 (benchmark kickoff)

Attachments (to Drive): benchmark-harness-template.yaml, run_repro.sh, Dockerfile, FR_prompt_seed_v1.jsonl

—
Karthik
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Diaz <alice.diaz@fastretail.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@fastretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 07 Mar 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: perf qualification kickoff — SLOs, prompt handoff, reproducibility

Hi Alice / Tom — thanks, we have visibility into the Drive folder and the sanitized 5k export is there (fastretail-prod-sample-sanitized.zip). I’ve kicked off the ingestion job and will post the ingestion log to the Drive folder when done.

Planned immediate steps (today):
- Ingest sample and validate schema (sanitization check).
- Run smoke replay against dev harness for the three critical flows (checkout, search, personalization).
- Generate an initial artifact bundle: harness-config.yaml, run-output-smoke.json, and perf-snapshot.png.

Tentative readout: Thu 03/09 10:00 AM PT — Karthik/Ben/Marissa will present smoke results and propose the full-run windows. If that time works, I’ll drop a calendar invite.

If anything unexpected shows up in the ingestion (missing tokens, PII residue) I’ll flag immediately.

—
Marissa Cole
Benchmark Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
